artboards.title: Permit fee revenue — the conflict is the output
What has to land, and who acts
Once the fund ledger lands — the target

annotations.text:
THE BRIEF, AND IT IS AN OPERATOR CORRECTION.
Removing the v1 fabrications is NOT the product. It is the gap analysis that tells us what to fill in to get to v2.
So this lens is drawn at its FULL SHAPE: every cell it will ever hold exists on the page from the start, each one either measured or countably unaccounted, and every unaccounted cell has a named acquisition path.
A missing column is invisible. An unaccounted cell is countable. That is the whole reason the empty states are drawn rather than omitted.

FOUR STATES, AND THEY ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE.
MEASURED - read from a source, carrying that source and the date.
UNACCOUNTED - the cell exists, nothing acquired. Legitimate at rest, fatal at publish.
REFUSED - a derived figure whose input is unaccounted. Not a zero.
CONFLICT - two independently derived readings disagree, and the disagreement is the output.
v1 has one state: a number. That is the defect, expressed once.

ACTUAL SPENT IS THE BUDGET COLUMN COPIED.
Capture pages 11-12: ten departments, ten identical Budget and Actual Spent pairs, 100% burn on every single one.
The product states it in a caution banner on that one sub-tab and then consumes the figures as measured everywhere else - including an alarm derived from the fabricated equality: "Non-Departmental is approaching budget cap at 100% - only $0 remaining."
Here: appropriation is read, actuals are unaccounted, and variance and burn are REFUSED. Four numbers become one honest absence.

AND THE ARTEFACT NOBODY WOULD CATCH.
The capture reports "Budget pace: 94% spent at 94% of fiscal year (+0% vs expected)."
Spent equals budget by construction, and elapsed drives the expectation, so the two track each other NECESSARILY and the variance is always zero. It is not a result, it is an identity.
A figure that cannot come out any other way is not a measurement, and it reads as the most reassuring number on the page.

A COLLECTION RATE OF 157% IS NOT A REACHABLE STATE.
Collected cannot exceed charged. v1 prints it in green with a success mark (capture page 23).
The surplus traces to ONE partition: Unassigned, read as collecting $450.9M against $170.9M charged - roughly $280M unattributed, and the second largest line in the breakdown.
The magnitudes are impossible for this city anyway: $664.7M collected against a $69.6M total operating budget, and $231,000 per permit on Building Department alone.

THE PERMIT COUNTS DO NOT TIE, AND THE TWO PAGES DISAGREE.
Header: 1,877 permits. Department rows sum to 3,138 on one capture page and 4,052 on another. Building Department is 1,055 permits on one and 1,970 on the other, with different totals to match.
Three populations, one label. The lens refuses the count rather than picking the one that looks right.

THE GAP AS A SURFACE, NOT A FOOTNOTE.
Four sources, what each unlocks, what has to be acquired, who acts. Three of the four rows have an owner who is not us, which is the point of naming them.
ONE source - the fund ledger - fills four regions that are refused today. It is the highest-leverage acquisition on the lens and it is a request to the city finance director, not a build.
An unaccounted cell with no named acquisition path is indistinguishable from a field nobody thought of.

THE MOST EXPENSIVE SHAPE IN v1.
The Scenario Modeler (capture pages 13-22) runs three-year projections with conservative / expected / optimistic ranges and stamps them HIGH CONFIDENCE, beside a 3/3 connected badge.
Its expense baseline is the budget column copied.
This is the screen a city manager takes into a council meeting. Confidence asserted about a simulation whose baseline was never measured is worse than no simulation, because it is actionable.

THE TARGET, AND IT IS LABELLED NOT TODAY.
The same lens with the fund ledger and department spend acquired. The cells that were unaccounted on the first artboard are exactly the cells that fill.
The appropriation column is read from the capture. Actuals, variance and burn are ILLUSTRATIVE and the basis line says so.
Note that burn VARIES here - 76% to 103%. Real burn varies. Every row identical at 100% is the tell, and it is what the capture shows.
